STEP 1 - Scene: A light meal of roasted chicken (a piece of chicken thigh or drumstick with visible herb seasoning) beside a small portion of fresh arugula/rocket salad. Photographed from above at a steep angle on a white plate on a wooden table.

STEP 2 - Ruler: White rectangular/square-ish plate, roughly 26 cm across the longer dimension. Area of an equivalent 26 cm round plate = 3.14 x 13^2 ≈ 530 cm². Only the visible portion of the plate is considered.

STEP 3 - Items: (a) roasted chicken piece (skin and meat, with a bone end visible at the top); (b) fresh arugula/rocket leaves, lightly dressed or plain.

STEP 4 - Area: Arugula covers roughly 8% of the plate (~42 cm²). Chicken piece at the top edge covers roughly 6% (~32 cm²), partly cropped by the frame.

STEP 5 - Volume: Arugula: 42 cm² x 3 cm ≈ 126 ml. Chicken: a single piece about 32 cm² x 1.5 cm ≈ 48 ml.

STEP 6 - Grams: Arugula: 126 ml x 0.15 ≈ 19 g. Chicken: 48 ml x 1.0 ≈ 48 g (cooked meat with skin).

STEP 7 - Energy: Arugula 19 g x 25 kcal/100 g ≈ 5 kcal. Roasted chicken with skin 48 g x 215 kcal/100 g ≈ 103 kcal.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: A small salad plus one visible piece of chicken (drumstick/thigh portion) totals roughly 67 g and about 108 kcal. The chicken piece is cropped at the top of the frame, so part of it may be off-image, which would raise the estimate somewhat. Plausible for the visible food.
